research_question: Can causal top-of-book bid/ask quoted-volume imbalance in the canonical Dukascopy XAUUSD tick feed provide a high-frequency entry edge that survives Coinexx-like P75 executable spread/costs?

sources.name: Gould & Bonart — Queue Imbalance as a One-Tick-Ahead Price Predictor in a Limit Order Book
sources.reconstruction: I=(bid_size-ask_size)/(bid_size+ask_size); sign predicts direction of next mid-price move; paper identifies a central regime around -0.25..0.25 and stronger practical forecasts away from zero.

sources.name: Stoikov — The Micro-Price: A High Frequency Estimator of Future Prices
sources.reconstruction: microprice/fair-price adjustment uses spread and bid/ask imbalance; used here as theoretical support for imbalance direction, not as a fitted model.

sources.name: Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov — The Price Impact of Order Book Events
sources.reconstruction: short-horizon price changes are strongly related to order-flow imbalance at best bid/ask; no fitted coefficients imported.

profiles.rule: enter on first causal tick entering |I|>=0.25; direction=sign(I)
enter on first causal tick entering |I|>=0.50; direction=sign(I)
enter on first causal tick entering |I|>=0.75; direction=sign(I)

event_semantics: A new event requires prior tick below the profile absolute-imbalance threshold or opposite sign; repeated ticks inside the same same-sign strong regime do not create duplicate proposals.

evaluation.economics: existing DELTA 30-second initial-hold execution: 0.01 lot, P75 BUY ask/SELL bid entry, protective stop 300 raw, trail activate 100 raw, trail distance 30 raw, max hold 30s, $0.01 entry + $0.01 exit commission

anti_overfit: If all fixed profiles fail executable economics, retire family even if one-tick classification is statistically positive.
